title: ArmTrailResult
description: Synchronous return value of PositionWorkflow.arm_trail. Echoes what was ACTUALLY armed rather than what was requested, because the workflow resolves the anchor itself when peak_premium is omitted — the operator needs to see the stop that now exists, not the one they asked for. REJECTED is the load-bearing case: it is what stops the UI reporting success for an arm that never happened.

status.description: ARMED: the trail is now live on this position. ALREADY_ARMED: a trail was already running and this request did not LOOSEN it (the workflow never widens an existing stop). REJECTED: nothing was armed — the position remains unprotected and `reason` says why.

reason.description: Why the arm was refused. Mirrors the existing ChandelierArmRejected reasons (invalid_peak, invalid_giveback) plus subscription_failed and anchor_unresolvable. Surfaced verbatim to the operator; absent when status != REJECTED.

peak_premium.description: The anchor the trail is actually pegged at — the workflow's resolved value, not necessarily the requested one. Absent on REJECTED.

giveback_pct.description: The giveback actually in force. On ALREADY_ARMED this is the PRE-EXISTING (tighter) value, not the requested one. Absent on REJECTED.

stop_price.description: peak_premium * (1 - giveback_pct) at arm time, so the UI can echo a concrete number without re-deriving the workflow's arithmetic. A LIVE value that rises with the peak — never render it as a fixed floor the operator set. Absent on REJECTED.
